quote:
A Fischer r–z test confirmed
that these correlations differed significantly (z = 2.6, p = .01).
reason: Primary source identity (Paxton, Ungar, & Greene, 2011, Cognitive Science, DOI 10.1111/j.1551-6709.2011.01210.x) and the Experiment 1 p. 4 Fisher r-to-z correlation comparison (z = 2.6, p = .01, comparing r = .39, p = .001 in CRT-First vs. r = -.03, p = .8 in Dilemmas-First) are confirmed. Shipped's inline sample annotation in 'Z = 2.6, N = 92' erroneously transfers the post-exclusion subsample (N = 92: n1 = 41 CRT-First, n2 = 51 Dilemmas-First) from the preceding means t-test, which would yield z = 2.03, p = .042 (and p = .012 for r = .39); the full pre-exclusion Experiment 1 sample of N = 150 (n1 = 65 CRT-First, n2 = 85 Dilemmas-First; see p. 4 counts, Fig. 1 plotting 65 CRT-First points including CRT score = 0, and p. 6 'Likewise, across all subjects') reproduces z = 2.63 (reported 2.6), p = .0087 (reported .01) and p = .0013 (reported .001) for r = .39, giving the corrected expression 'Z = 2.6, N = 150'.
